subject: maths
title: Addition and Subtraction - Pairs and Differences
introductionText:
Term 2 · Number
Addition and Subtraction — Pairs and
Differences
The Big Idea: Pairs that make 10 are the most useful facts in maths. The difference
between two numbers is how many steps it takes to get from the smaller one to the
bigger one.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"Hold up 10 fingers. Fold down 3. How many are still up? 7. So 3 and 7 are partners —
together they make 10. The partners are: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. To
find the difference between 6 and 9, put your finger on 6 and count on to 9: seven, eight,
nine. Three jumps. The difference is 3."
Watch Out For
The slip almost every child makes
Silly answers nobody checks. He writes 6 + 3 = 19 and moves on. Teach him to estimate
first: "Both numbers are small — can the answer be nearly 20?"
Counting the start number when finding a difference. Same slip as Unit 2 — count the
jumps, not the numbers you touch.
Try It at Home
Game 1 — Shake and make ten (10 minutes)
Put 10 dried beans in a cup: some white, some brown (or chickpeas and lentils). Shake
and tip into an egg box, one per hole. "How many white? How many brown? Say the
pair." Keep a list of every pair you find. Can you find a pair you haven't seen yet?
Game 2 — What's under the cup? (5 minutes)
Count out 10 beans together. While he closes his eyes, hide some under a cup. He counts
what's left and works out how many are hiding. Lift the cup to check. Later, use 15 or 20
beans.
Pairs that make 10 in a ten frame
9 + 1 = 10 7 + 3 = 10 5 + 5 = 10
Cover the orange dots with your hand and ask how many are hiding. Then do the same with the blue.
More examples to talk about
• 10 + 0 = 10 and 0 + 10 = 10 are pairs too.
• 5 + 5 is the only pair where both partners are the same.
• If 3 + 2 = 5, then 13 + 2 = 15. The ones work the same way in the teens.
• Tricky: the difference between 12 and 15 is 3 — the same as between 2 and 5.
• Tricky: 9 + 8 must be close to 20, not close to 10. Estimating catches mistakes.
Key Words
total pairs make ten difference estimate number line

What is the difference between 5 and 9?
Sam says 6 + 3 = 19. Is that sensible? What is the right answer?
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: No. Both numbers are small, so the answer can't be near 20. 6 + 3 = 9.
